roadmap.goal: Story #5913 — retire the Faster Updates switch and make the two-step refresh the only refresh wherever the connector can scan. Two production moves, each with the test rework it forces in the same commit: (1) the refresh stops reading the switch — SyncModeResolver.Resolve loses its opt-in parameter and leading Full branch, WorkItemService loses TheOperatorAskedForTheCheaperRefresh() and its IRepository<OptionalFeature> dependency, and all three fetch deciders (team, portfolio Features, parent Features) always scan; (2) the switch itself goes — OptionalFeatureSeeder moves DeltaSyncKey into RemoveDeprecatedFeatures and stops seeding it, so an instance that had it on or off loses the row at start-up and never gets it back. Then the user-facing docs stop describing a toggle. Done when: all seven Story5913AlwaysFasterUpdatesTest cases are un-ignored and green; `grep -rn "operatorAskedForTheCheaperRefresh\|TheOperatorAskedForTheCheaperRefresh" Lighthouse.Backend` returns zero matches; `dotnet build` has zero warnings; the backend suite is green with `--filter "TestCategory!=Integration&TestCategory!=JiraIntegration&TestCategory!=LinearIntegration&TestCategory!=AdoIntegration&TestCategory!=ServiceNowIntegration"`; `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` are green with zero warnings. Mutation testing (Stryker.NET >= 80% on the changed lines of SyncModeResolver, WorkItemService's three fetch deciders and OptionalFeatureSeeder) is a later gate the maintainer approves separately, run on frozen code after review — it is deliberately NOT a step here.
roadmap.paradigm_note: The Hypothesis + state-delta unit mandate from nw-roadmap does not apply here and its omission is deliberate, not an oversight. This repository is C# + NUnit 4.6 + Moq (backend) and TypeScript + Vitest + RTL (frontend); there is no pytest-bdd, no .feature file and no Hypothesis. DISTILL recorded it (feature-delta.md, DISTILL / Reconciliation and the mandate-compliance note under Upstream findings): layer 3+ acceptance, example-only, the one finite axis (on/off) expressed as an NUnit [TestCase]. The crafter authors NO new acceptance tests in this story — the seven Story5913 cases were written by DISTILL and sit [Ignore(PendingDeliver)]. The crafter's RED phase is un-ignoring them and watching them fail exactly as red-classification.md recorded; its GREEN phase is production code. The only tests the crafter edits or deletes are the ones DISTILL's Existing-test disposition table lists, each in the same commit as the production change that makes it wrong, so no commit is red.

user_decisions: D1 — an instance that had Faster Updates off gets it on. The DeltaSync row is removed; a previous 'off' is no longer honoured, and the release notes say so plainly. No startup warning.

D2 — no kill switch. No config key, no environment variable, no hidden setting replaces the toggle. The only safety net is the existing one: a failed or refused identity scan downloads the whole query and logs a WARNING.
D3 — KPI-3 accepted on the dev instance's evidence (118 delta refreshes, none unsuccessful, every failed scan fell back to Full).
D4 — the removal is done by the seeder, not by a migration. DeltaSyncKey joins RemoveDeprecatedFeatures; the constant stays because the deprecated list names it. No schema change.
D5 — the `Update completed | … | mode=… | scanned=… | fetched=…` log line does not change. Only the docs' advice to 'turn the toggle off to compare' goes.
D6 — user-facing text uses the configurable terms (Work Item, Feature). No new UI strings; the change removes a row and adds none.
out_of_scope: A kill switch in any form (D2), and a startup warning for instances that had it off (D1).
Deleting the OptionalFeatureKeys.DeltaSyncKey constant (D4). It stays, reworded.
Any change to the update log line (D5) or to SyncOutcome — including SyncOutcome.DeltaSync, which shares the name and nothing else.
Any change to the removal rule (stored − swept), staleness evaluation or the fetch fingerprint (ADR-138/140/141).
Delta refresh for ServiceNow, Linear or CSV. They answer SupportsIncrementalSync = false and keep refreshing in full.

Any frontend production change. BehaviourSettingsTable renders whatever the endpoint returns; no production file names DeltaSync. SystemSettingsTab.behaviourSettings.test.tsx was already renamed off DeltaSync at DISTILL.
Any EF migration. The seeder removes the row; the expand-only migration rule is not in play.

A new port-level acceptance scenario for 'a first refresh falls back to Full' (DISTILL Upstream finding 1). The crafter authors no tests; it stays covered by SyncModeResolverTest and exercised as a Given everywhere.

Finalize-time items, not DELIVER steps: the release-notes line on the ADO story (DoD 6, the story carries the Release Notes tag); regenerating docs/assets/settings/optionalfeatures.png (DoD 7) — the next @screenshot run shows the list one row shorter; ADO state transitions (the orchestrator's, Resolved on push, Closed on CI green — #5913 is a Story, so it does close).
Stryker mutation testing — a later gate, separately approved, on frozen code.

phases.name: Every refresh that can be cheap is cheap, without anyone asking
phases.description: Stop reading the switch, then remove the switch, then stop documenting it. The order matters: removing the row alone would make the refresh read 'no row' as off (TheOperatorAskedForTheCheaperRefresh answers false on a missing row) and turn every instance's refresh back to Full. So the read goes first, and scenarios 4-6 prove it; the row goes second, and scenarios 1-3 prove it.
